findings.claim: purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser is the PR's only test for the new user_location cleanup in HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation, and it passes verbatim when that cleanup is deleted, so it does not exercise the behaviour it was added for.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is the join-row cleanup is unguarded: any later edit that drops it or moves it after session.remove ships green, and purgeLocation then fails at transaction commit in production with a referential-integrity violation on user_location(location_id), because the one test that exists to catch exactly that cannot fail. The break is invisible to CI, so the cost of discovery lands on whoever purges a location in a deployment that has populated user_location.
findings.evidence: Ran on b7cd909 (JAVA_HOME=jdk-21, mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest='LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation*'): 4/4 green. Then deleted the two added lines (the native 'delete from user_location where location_id = :locationId' plus setParameter) from HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation and re-ran the same selection: still 4/4 green, BUILD SUCCESS. Mechanism, measured with a temporary probe in the same class: LocationService.purgeLocation -> HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation -> session.remove(location), and LocationServiceTest's assertion goes through HibernateLocationDAO.getLocation(Integer) = session.get(Location.class, id), which returns null for a session-removed entity with no SQL DELETE issued ('PROBEA assertNull sees: null'); BaseContextSensitiveTest rolls the transaction back, so the FK is never evaluated. A discriminating shape does exist and I ran it: save the assignment, Context.flushSession(), Context.clearSession(), reload location 4, purgeLocation, Context.flushSession() -- 'PROBEB purge+flush SUCCEEDED' with the fix present, and with the fix removed 'PROBEB purge+flush THREW org.h2.jdbc.JdbcBatchUpdateException: Referential integrity constraint violation: "FKC0WEUGWTYIDBYTMDYE09CP0GL: PUBLIC.USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES PUBLIC.LOCATION(LOCATION_ID) (4)"'. Note for whoever writes the repair: the clearSession/reload step is required, not cosmetic -- adding a bare Context.flushSession() to the test as written throws 'TransientPropertyValueException: Persistent instance of org.openmrs.User references an unsaved transient instance of org.openmrs.Location [org.openmrs.User.locations -> org.openmrs.Location]' even WITH the fix, because the test still holds the session-cached User that references the removed Location (the condition HibernateLocationDAO.java:129 hedges on). Asserting the join row is gone (select count(*) from user_location) is the other workable assertion; the probe confirmed it goes 1 -> 0 with the fix.

findings.claim: The deliberate re-read of the user ('re-read the user so the lazy collection initialises inside this transaction, whatever the caller passed in') is not covered: all five new getAllowedLocations tests pass when dao.getUser(user.getUserId()) is replaced by the caller's own object, because every test hands in a User fetched inside the same Hibernate session with its locations set in memory.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, the only reason for the extra round-trip is a code comment, and the test suite says it is dead weight. Remove it (an obvious target for a later simplify pass) and the primary intended caller breaks with no test failing: getAllowedLocations(Context.getAuthenticatedUser(), tag) -- the login-location use case the ticket is about -- throws LazyInitializationException, because the authenticated User is held across requests and is detached, and a caller that passes a synthetic User(id) instead silently receives EVERY tagged location for a user restricted to one, i.e. the exact over-permission the feature exists to prevent, with no exception for CI to see.
findings.evidence: Replaced 'dao.getUser(user.getUserId())' with 'user' on UserServiceImpl.java:860 and ran mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest='UserServiceTest#getAllowedLocations*' -> Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, BUILD SUCCESS (all five new tests pass without the re-read). Two temporary probes in UserServiceTest, same setup in both (tagLocations(1,2); assignLocations(2); Context.flushSession(); Context.clearSession()): (a) getAllowedLocations(new User(1), tag) returns size 1 -> [2] with the re-read and size 2 -> [1, 2] without it; (b) getAllowedLocations(Context.getAuthenticatedUser(), tag) returns size 1 -> [2] with the re-read and 'THREW org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: Cannot lazily initialize collection of role org.openmrs.User.locations with key 1 (no session)' without it. Either probe, added as a real test, would be the missing guard. Restored with git checkout; no in-repo consumer of getAllowedLocations exists (git grep over the tree finds only the declaration, the impl and the tests), so the tests are the whole contract.

findings.claim: @Independent on User.locations is load-bearing and has no test, while the repo already has exactly this test for both of the other two @Independent fields in the codebase.
findings.evidence: User implements Retireable (User.java:69) and RequiredDataAdvice.before:181 calls recursivelyHandle(RetireHandler.class, ...) for retire* methods, with the @Independent skip at RequiredDataAdvice.java:306. Measured: a temporary probe that assigns locations 1 and 2 to user 1 then calls userService.retireUser(user, 'probe reason') prints 'loc1 retired=false loc2 retired=false' on b7cd909 and 'loc1 retired=true loc2 retired=true' with @Independent removed from User.java:110 -- so removing it makes retiring a user retire every location that user is assigned to. With @Independent removed, mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest='UserServiceTest,LocationServiceTest,UserTest,HibernateUserDAOTest' still reports Tests run: 223, Failures: 0, BUILD SUCCESS, i.e. nothing in the User/Location test area detects the removal. The project's own convention covers the other two: LocationServiceTest.java:1218 retireLocation_shouldNotRetireIndependentField (Location.tags) and OrderServiceTest.java:3316 retireOrderType_shouldNotRetireIndependentField (OrderType.conceptClasses). A retireUser_shouldNotRetireIndependentField mirroring those is a four-line test.

findings.claim: The new user_location FK constrains deletion from both ends, and only the location end has a test; nothing exercises purging a user that has assigned locations.
findings.evidence: A temporary probe (assign location 1 to user 501, saveUser, flushSession, purgeUser, flushSession) prints 'PROBE purgeUser+flush SUCCEEDED' on b7cd909, so no production change is needed today -- Hibernate deletes the owning side's join rows with the User. The gap is that the behaviour is unpinned: purgeUser_shouldDeleteGivenUser (UserServiceTest.java:1054) never assigns locations, so a later mapping change (making the association inverse, or moving ownership to a Location-side collection) would reintroduce the referential-integrity failure on the user side with nothing failing. The probe above, dropped in next to purgeUser_shouldDeleteGivenUser with a flush, is the test.

findings.claim: User.getLocations() -- the accessor the new Javadoc points readers at -- has no test of its own, and off-session it throws rather than returning the empty set the Javadoc describes; is detached access meant to be in contract?
findings.evidence: A temporary probe (assignLocations(1,2); flushSession; clearSession; u = userService.getUser(1); Context.evictFromSession(u); u.getLocations().size()) prints 'THREW org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException: Cannot lazily initialize collection of role org.openmrs.User.locations with key 1 (no session)'. The sibling @ManyToMany on the same entity, roles (User.java:95-99), is FetchType.EAGER and additionally second-level cached, so this collection behaves differently from the one it is modelled on; User is @Audited, @Cacheable and Serializable, and Context.getAuthenticatedUser() hands out an instance held across requests. Coverage of locations today runs only through UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations, which re-reads inside a read-only transaction and therefore never touches the getter's documented contract on a detached instance. If detached access is intended to work, the collection needs a test (and probably EAGER or an explicit fetch); if it is not, the Javadoc at User.java:101-106 should say the getter must be called inside a session.

findings.claim: getAllowedLocations_shouldReturnAllTaggedLocationsIfTheUserHasNoAssignedLocations asserts only a count and never pins its own precondition, so it silently stops testing the unrestricted branch if user 1 ever gains assigned locations in the standard dataset.
findings.evidence: The body is tagLocations(1, 2) then assertThat(allowed, hasSize(2)) -- no assertion that userService.getUser(1).getLocations() is empty, and no assertion on which locations came back. Its sibling at line 1814 does pin the ids (assertEquals(Integer.valueOf(2), allowed.get(0).getLocationId())), and the intersection logic is genuinely covered: replacing the filter with 'return tagged' fails 2 of the 5 (getAllowedLocations_shouldReturnOnlyTheAssignedLocationsThatCarryTheTag:1826 and getAllowedLocations_shouldReturnAnEmptyListIfNoAssignedLocationCarriesTheTag:1835), so this is only about making the unrestricted branch's test self-describing. The first assertion inside the line-1814 test (hasSize(2) after tagging 1,2 and assigning 1,2,3) produces the same count as the unrestricted case and carries no information the second half does not already carry.

what_i_swept: Enumerated every behaviour change in the 8-file diff and tried to name a test for each, then mutation-tested each named test to see whether it can actually fail. Changes and verdicts: (1) HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation join-row cleanup -> the new LocationServiceTest test is vacuous, proven by reverting the fix and re-running (finding 1); (2) UserService/UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations -> five new tests, intersection and the tag-null/not-persisted guards genuinely covered (mutation-confirmed), the documented user re-read not covered (finding 2); (3) User.locations mapping + @Independent -> the annotation is load-bearing and unguarded (finding 3); (4) User.getLocations/setLocations accessors -> setter exercised only via the new tests, getter never tested and throws off-session (finding 5); (5) the liquibase user_location changeset -> genuinely covered, by ValidateHibernateMappingsDatabaseIT (mapping-vs-schema, mutation-confirmed) and DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT (ran, 917 correct); (6) the LOCATION_ID constant extraction -> covered by existing green tests. Established the test infrastructure first rather than assuming it: BaseContextSensitiveTest builds its H2 schema from hbm2ddl create-drop (BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:336), so the join table and its FKs in the default suite come from the annotations, while the DatabaseIT family builds from liquibase; CI runs both (.github/workflows/build.yaml matrix '' and '-Pintegration-test -Pskip-default-test') and neither leg sets useInMemoryDatabase=false. Outward trace: git grep for in-repo consumers of getAllowedLocations and User.getLocations (none besides the impl, so the tests are the whole contract and the REST consumer is in another repo); the other end of the new FK, purgeUser with assigned locations (probed, works, untested -> finding 4); the retire/void lifecycle reached through RequiredDataAdvice.before:181 and its @Independent skip at :306; the envers path, since User is @Audited (EnversAuditTableInitializerDatabaseIT checks entity audit tables only -> out of scope); the OpenmrsTestsTest meta-test's naming rule, which the new tests satisfy; and the project's own precedent for this exact test shape in LocationServiceTest:1218 and OrderServiceTest:3316.
out_of_scope: HibernateLocationDAO.java:129 hedges that a session-cached User.locations goes stale across the native delete; measured, it is worse than stale -- flushing after purgeLocation while a loaded User still references the removed Location throws TransientPropertyValueException, not a stale read. Correctness reviewer's call.

User is @Audited (envers) and the new locations collection carries no @NotAudited, unlike userProperties; the changeset creates no user_location audit table. Envers is off by default (hibernate.default.properties: hibernate.integration.envers.enabled=false, suffix _audit) and EnversAuditTableInitializer may create it at boot, but EnversAuditTableInitializerDatabaseIT only checks entity-level audit tables, not collection tables. Schema/correctness reviewer.

The 'assigned == null' guard in UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations is unreachable through the re-read path -- Hibernate never returns a null collection for a mapped Set -- so it is dead defensive code. Simplify territory, not coverage.

Nothing asserts that @Authorized(PrivilegeConstants.GET_LOCATIONS) is enforced on getAllowedLocations, but no sibling read method on UserService has such a test either, so the interesting question is the privilege choice itself (GET_LOCATIONS vs a user-scoped privilege, and whether any authenticated user may read another user's allowed locations). Security reviewer.

The liquibase table has a composite (user_id, location_id) primary key and no surrogate user_location_id column, where TRUNK-6669 proposes an auto-increment surrogate key; the JPA @JoinTable does not need one, but it is a deliberate divergence from the ticket. Schema reviewer.

TRUNK-6669's acceptance criteria are mostly about GET/POST/DELETE /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location, which live in openmrs-module-webservices.rest; this repo has no consumer of getAllowedLocations at all, so the end-to-end criteria are structurally untestable here. Solution-fit reviewer.
could_not_verify: Whether any test outside the four classes I ran (UserServiceTest, LocationServiceTest, UserTest, HibernateUserDAOTest -- 223 tests) would fail if @Independent were removed from User.locations. I did not run the full api suite; the claim in finding 3 is scoped to those classes plus the observation that the two existing @Independent guards target other fields.

Whether any of this differs on MySQL or PostgreSQL. Every run used the default in-memory H2 path (useInMemoryDatabase defaults true, hbm2ddl create-drop) plus the DatabaseIT H2 path, which is also all CI exercises (.github/workflows/build.yaml has no -DuseInMemoryDatabase=false leg). The mechanism behind finding 1 (session.get returning null for a removed entity, plus rollback without flush) is engine-independent, but I did not reproduce it on a container DB.
notes: Diff stat verified before reviewing: git diff 28e3bab..b7cd909 = 8 files, 216 insertions, 6 deletions -- matches the brief. The brief's javaCompilerVersion=1.8 note does not apply to this repo (pom.xml:813 sets maven.compiler.release=21); every run used JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-21.jdk, mvn -o -pl api test with narrow -Dtest selections, never install. Two candidate findings were killed by experiment and are deliberately absent. (a) 'The liquibase changeset is never cross-checked against the JPA mapping, because the default test schema is hbm2ddl create-drop.' Refuted: renaming the changeset's location_id column to loc_id makes ValidateHibernateMappingsDatabaseIT fail with 'SchemaManagementException: Schema validation: missing column [location_id] in table [user_location]' (it builds the schema from every liquibase snapshot/update combination, then boots with hbm2ddl.auto=validate), and that IT runs in CI via the integration-test profile's integration-test-2 execution. It passes on b7cd909 as shipped. (b) 'The intersection is only asserted by counts, so it is not really covered.' Refuted: replacing the filter with 'return tagged' fails 2 of the 5 new tests. Also verified positively rather than assumed: DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT passes at 917, so the constant bump is right; each of the five Should clauses added to the UserService Javadoc has a matching test method; and the three call sites touched by the LOCATION_ID constant extraction in HibernateLocationDAO are covered by existing green tests (LocationServiceTest/HibernateLocationDAOTest getLocationsHavingAllTags_*, LocationServiceTest getLocations_withDescendantOf_* at 1231+). 'Would fail on base' for the six new tests is trivially true by compilation: git show 28e3bab of User.java and UserService.java contains no setLocations/Set and no getAllowedLocations (positive control: the same grep pipeline finds setRoles in base User.java). All mutations and probes were reverted with git checkout -- ; git status --porcelain is empty in the worktree.
